rationale: Use a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and identify poorly resolved pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to tune selectivity in either direction.

Reduce gradient steepness to test whether the unresolved pair gains resolution while preserving the already resolved pairs. The initial run's 8.30-minute last peak suggests this modest extension may still keep all peaks near or below 10 minutes.

Shift the starting organic fraction upward while keeping nearly the same gradient slope as injection 2, which resolved every pair. This should bring the last peak below 10 minutes while largely preserving the critical pair's resolution.

Use a shallower gradient to lift the critical pair above R = 1.5, while raising the starting organic fraction to offset the added retention time. The early peaks have ample separation, making this a promising route to full resolution with the last peak below 10 minutes.

The maximum CRF is already achieved; this run tests whether it can be maintained with earlier elution. Raising the starting organic fraction should shorten retention, while the slightly shallower gradient should help preserve the critical pair's resolution.

Slightly flatten injection 5's gradient to recover resolution of the critical pair, using its nearly one-minute margin before the time penalty. This tests another route to CRF 1.000 while retaining injection 4 as the established optimum.

Test a modest temperature increase from injection 4 to shorten the fully resolved separation and measure the critical pair's temperature sensitivity. The maximum CRF is already secured, so this explores a faster method with the same score.

Test whether further heating carries the critical pair through an elution-order reversal and restores separation while shortening retention. Keep the gradient unchanged to isolate temperature-driven selectivity changes and check for new close pairs.

Slightly lengthen the gradient to try to resolve the new limiting pair at 55 C, using the 1.46-minute margin before the time penalty. Monitor the reordered central peaks as well, since their resolution may respond differently to the shallower slope.

Use a gradient slope between injections 8 and 9 to target full resolution with a shorter separation than injection 9. The limiting pair is predicted to remain just above R = 1.5, with the last peak around 9 minutes.

Test a lower starting organic fraction to improve separation of the limiting central pair, combined with a steeper gradient to shorten the run. This explores a faster fully resolved method while retaining the already demonstrated CRF 1.000 methods.

Shorten injection 11's gradient to test whether full resolution can be retained with the last peak below 8 minutes. The reordered critical pair has tolerated steeper gradients at 55 C, while the other close pair has some resolution margin.

Choose a gradient slope between injections 11 and 12, targeting recovery of the limiting pair to R ≥ 1.5 with the last peak around 8 minutes. The lower endpoint remains well above the observed elution window, so all peaks should still elute during the gradient.

Slightly steepen injection 13's gradient to seek an earlier last peak while retaining full resolution. Interpolation from injections 12 and 13 predicts the two closest pairs will remain just above R = 1.5.

Test the upper temperature limit with injection 14's gradient to map further selectivity changes and shorten retention. The close pairs may reorder or lose resolution, but the maximum CRF is already secured by several methods.

Explore lower-temperature selectivity with a short gradient as an alternative route to a faster fully resolved separation. Cooling may separate the temperature-sensitive central pair, but the full table will be checked for new overlaps or elution-order changes.

Return to the successful 55 C region and test whether a lower starting organic fraction permits a steeper, faster gradient by improving the limiting pair's selectivity. Monitor both close central pairs, since improving one may reduce the other's resolution.

Test whether a much steeper gradient at 60 C moves the coeluting pair seen in injection 15 through a selectivity reversal into a resolved, faster regime. This is exploratory; injection 17 already provides full resolution and the maximum CRF with a 7.60-minute last peak.

Test a shallower gradient with a higher starting organic fraction to spread the compressed central cluster while shifting selectivity away from the overlap seen at 60 C. This explores a substantially faster separation, with the established maximum-score methods retained as fallbacks.

Raise the starting organic fraction to test whether selectivity shifts can resolve injection 19's remaining close pair while maintaining rapid elution. Check the first two peaks carefully, since their separation may deteriorate as initial retention decreases.

Trim injection 17's gradient endpoint while preserving its exact slope and starting composition. The last peak previously eluted near 0.57 organic, so this method should reproduce full resolution and CRF 1.000 while reaching the final hold sooner.

Test the next steeper practical gradient near injection 21 to locate the speed limit for full resolution at 55 C. This should shorten retention, although the closely spaced central pairs may fall below R = 1.5; maximum-score methods are already established.

Explore a steeper gradient at the untested intermediate temperature of 50 C, seeking a faster separation with a different central-peak selectivity pattern. The low starting organic fraction protects early retention, while the established CRF 1.000 methods remain available.

Return to the established maximum-score region with a slightly shallower gradient than injection 13, seeking more separation of its slope-sensitive close pair. The last peak should remain comfortably below 10 minutes, while the other central pair is expected to retain full resolution.

Use nearly the same slope as injection 9, which achieved CRF 1.000 with both critical pairs at R = 1.70, while trimming the endpoint above the last peak's elution composition. This should preserve full resolution and a last peak below 10 minutes with a shorter programmed gradient.
